subject: Order form: IP indemnity, evidence custodian & notice window
messages:
From: Alice Moran <alice.moran@lumenhealth.com>
To: markus_klein@redwoodinference.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com, procurement@lumenhealth.com
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA redlines - IP indemnity carveouts and notice timing

Markus / Kimberly,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the draft order form. Procurement ran the redline with our legal team and we have a couple of material asks on the IP indemnity section that we need to surface before we can approve the order form. Attached is a redline with our requested edits. High level: 1) customer must be able to control the defense for third-party IP claims and select outside counsel; 2) notice window for claims should be 30 days from becoming reasonably aware; 3) we are proposing an explicit carveout for model-generated outputs where the customer can seek reimbursement only if the customer supplies the specific training data or prompt causing the alleged infringement.

We understand Redwood's position on defend vs reimburse and proposed caps; we can be flexible if we get stronger notice obligations, quick evidence access, and a named evidence custodian for the first 90 days of triage. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a 30-day notice window and accept customer control of the defense with the ability for Redwood to participate?

Attachments: LumenHealth-MSA-redline.docx

Next steps: procurement needs an answer this week to keep the renewal timetable.

Thanks,

Alice Moran
Senior Contracts Manager | LumenHealth
alice.moran@lumenhealth.com

Subject: Re: MSA redlines - IP indemnity carveouts and notice timing

Alice —

Appreciate the clear summary and the redline. We can (and want to) move quickly to close this. High-level response: we cannot accept open-ended defend-control for claims that arise from model outputs where the underlying allegation requires proof tied to Redwood training data. However we can propose a compromise to unblock procurement: 1) 60-day notice window (we believe 30 days is often impracticable for large enterprise triage across teams); 2) Redwood will defend third-party IP claims for covered products unless the claim relates solely to customer-provided content or to model outputs where the customer has not provided the necessary evidence (training data or prompts) to verify the allegation — in those cases, we offer a reimbursement path; 3) for the first 90 days after notice we agree to an evidence custodian arrangement: customer retains primary custody but Redwood will have read-only access to the triage bundle (logs, prompts, outputs) under a mutual NDA for investigation purposes; 4) insurance offset and standard cap remain but we can talk about a modest increase to the defense cap for strategic customers.

I've attached our proposed redline (Redwood-proposed-redline.docx) with exact language for the defend/reimburse split and the evidence-custodian workflow. If that aligns with LumenHealth's risk tolerance, Kimberly (cc'd) will formalize the tweak into the order form amendment.

Proposed immediate next step: can we get a call tomorrow morning to walk through the defend/reimburse example scenarios so we can align counsel? If procurement is pressed for timelines, we can also provide a short MOU (1 page) that locks in the compromise while legal finishes the order form edits.

Best,

Markus Klein
Director, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MSA redlines - IP indemnity carveouts and notice timing

Team —

Following Markus' summary, I drafted a short patch to the order form that operationalizes the evidence custodian approach and the defend/reimburse boundary. Key points in the draft language:

- Notice timing: 60 days from the date the recipient becomes reasonably aware of the claim; parties should use commercially reasonable efforts to provide earlier notice where practicable.
- Defend vs reimburse: Redwood will assume defense for third-party IP claims that (a) allege infringement of rights in pre-existing customer content provided to Redwood, or (b) relate to Redwood platform code or model weights. Allegations that rely primarily on model outputs where verification depends on customer-supplied training data or prompts will be eligible for reimbursement unless the customer supplies the evidence within 30 days of request.
- Evidence custodian: for the first 90 days after notice, the submitting party (usually customer) will be the evidence custodian and must provide a triage bundle (logs, prompts, outputs). Redwood will be allowed read-only access under a mutual confidentiality addendum. If evidence is not provided in good faith within 30 days of request, cost-shifting applies.

Questions for LumenHealth: 1) Do you have a preferred counsel selection process (outside counsel panel, hourly guidelines) if the customer insists on control? 2) Do you require an explicit insurance representation (carrier + limits + expiration) as a pre-sign condition? 3) Are you ok with the 60-day notice in exchange for the evidence custodian and read-only access?

If you prefer, we can convert these bullets into mark-up language for direct insertion into the order form.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com

Date: Thu, 28 Jun 2028 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA redlines - IP indemnity carveouts and notice timing

Kimberly / Markus —

Thanks for the detailed proposal. A few quick answers and clarifications from LumenHealth legal/procurement:

- Counsel selection: LumenHealth needs to retain primary control of the defense for third-party IP claims; we will allow Redwood to participate and to approve counsel if there's a clear conflict interest. Our standard outside counsel panel is acceptable — I can send over the panel and hourly caps.
- Insurance: procurement requires a certificate of insurance showing commercial general liability and cyber coverage; we can accept carrier/language redaction for public release but need the carrier name and limit for underwriting.
- Notice: 60 days is acceptable provided the evidence custodian mechanism is robust. We will commit to producing the triage bundle within 30 days of a documented request; however, we will push back on any clause that creates an automatic cost-shift if the bundle requires internal approvals to produce (legal/clinical).

I've attached our SOC2 Type II summary for your security team and the procurement PO referenced earlier. If you can update the redline with the counsel selection flow and an explicit insurance representation, procurement can sign off pending legal's final language.

Regards,

Alice Moran
Senior Contracts Manager | LumenHealth
alice.moran@lumenhealth.com
